name: Postmodern feminism
summary: Postmodern feminism applies poststructuralist ideas from Derrida and Foucault to feminism, holding that gender, and for Butler sex too, is produced by language, norms and power rather than given by nature. It rejects a single essential 'woman', a universal women's experience and any neutral view from nowhere, favouring situated knowledge, difference, and coalitions built on affinity rather than shared identity. Its explicit politics is thin, but it is generally left-leaning, anti-militarist and sceptical of both unitary programmes and state control.
scope: The profile represents the academic strand running from the French feminists (Cixous, Irigaray, Kristeva) through Judith Butler's Gender Trouble and Donna Haraway's cyborg writing, as summarized by Wikipedia and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Because the school is a theory of identity, language and knowledge rather than a political programme, most answers on economics, constitutions and foreign policy are inferred from Haraway's socialist-feminist and anti-militarist writing and Butler's public positions, and carry low confidence. It excludes radical, liberal and Marxist feminisms.

keyFigures.name: Judith Butler
keyFigures.role: Philosopher whose Gender Trouble argues gender is performative and that sex is also constructed

keyFigures.name: Donna Haraway
keyFigures.role: Theorist of the cyborg and situated knowledges; argued for affinity rather than identity

keyFigures.name: Hélène Cixous
keyFigures.role: French feminist theorist associated with the school's psychoanalytic and linguistic strand

public-ownership.rationale: The school is wary of both privatization (Haraway) and centralized command-control structures, so adherents have no settled view on state ownership.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Haraway criticizes corporate high-tech and privatization as forms of domination, implying support for tighter regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Haraway describes the dismantling of the welfare state as feeding the feminization of poverty, so cutting welfare runs against the school's analysis.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist-feminist heritage leans toward worker control, but postmodern feminists distrust totalizing blueprints, so no firm answer.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Haraway names surveillance and command-control technology as core instruments of the informatics of domination; Foucauldian suspicion of self-surveillance reinforces this.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Butler questions the state's power to define hate speech and warns that censorship is complex, so adherents lean against statutory restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: Postmodern feminism rejects centralized authority and the single viewpoint, and treats power as diffuse; a leader bypassing deliberation is contrary to that.

state-harmful.rationale: Foucault sees power as dispersed rather than located in the state, so this statement is not their framing; mild disagreement.

empower-police-military.rationale: Haraway criticizes militarization and command-control as drivers of domination; Butler critiques policing, so more funding runs against the school.

decide-locally.rationale: The school stresses situated knowledge but offers no view on the level of government.

traditional-family.rationale: Haraway argues that the traditional nuclear family is being displaced and rejects organicist wholeness, and Butler treats kinship norms as constructed.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Butler's critique of the heterosexual matrix supports equal recognition, though some queer theorists also doubt marriage itself, so not strong.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The article states that gender is socially constructed and Butler goes further, holding that sex is constructed through language too.

gradual-change.rationale: The tradition aims at destabilizing established categories, though Butler stresses subversion from within; not framed in pace terms.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Haraway fears global command-control systems while favouring broad coalitions; no clear position.

nation-first.rationale: The school rejects natural identities and favours affinity across borders, so national-interest-first is not its stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Haraway embraces technology but warns it is also an informatics of domination, so she does not expect it to solve everything.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Haraway links high-tech militarism to domination; nuclear power itself is not covered.

revolution-justified.rationale: Butler favours nonviolence as an ethical position, but the tradition is also radical; the sources show no consensus.

experts-over-public.rationale: The school denies neutral expert knowledge: Haraway's situated knowledges mean no vantage point, expert or otherwise, is a view from nowhere.

central-planning.rationale: Haraway treats command-control hierarchy as a mode of domination and rejects totalizing theories, so central planning is disfavoured.

land-value-tax.rationale: None of the sources connects postmodern feminism to land taxation, so adherents have no distinctive position and the answer is neutral.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist protectionism cuts against the school's anti-essentialist, boundary-crossing politics.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Haraway's suspicion of command-control makes state direction of strategic industry unattractive.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Haraway discusses the homework economy but sets out no abolition of money or wages.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies imposing unity conflict with the anti-totalizing, affinity-based politics Haraway advocates.

one-party-rule.rationale: Postmodern feminism rejects a single correct viewpoint and grand narratives, so a party guided by the correct ideology is contrary to it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule rests on natural-order claims that the school's anti-essentialism rejects.

democracy-best.rationale: Butler defends assembly and democratic politics, though the school also critiques liberal democratic universalism.

natural-rulers.rationale: The school's anti-essentialism denies that traits are fixed by nature; the article describes its rejection of natural, fixed identities and the neutral perspective.

political-violence-never.rationale: Butler argues for nonviolence as an ethical position, but others in the tradition are not pacifist; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Haraway treats militarism as an instrument of domination and Butler argues for nonviolence.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Appealing to a single authoritative text conflicts with the rejection of grand narratives and universal truths.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Haraway criticizes privatization and militarization; privately provided coercion is the opposite of her politics.

military-superiority.rationale: Haraway criticizes high-tech military buildup as part of the informatics of domination.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Haraway holds that unity should rest on affinity, not natural identity, and rejects organic origins, so a nation defined by ethnic descent is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Haraway says Marxist and socialist-feminist accounts still carry a Western humanist self and rejects a single master narrative of history.

civilizational-union.rationale: Unity based on shared civilization is an identity-based claim the school distrusts.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Haraway stresses affinity, responsibility and partial connection, which clash with an ethic of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The school is sceptical of universal rights language, but it does not subordinate individuals to community duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Haraway rejects both the domination of nature and organicist appeals to natural wholeness; split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Haraway embraces technology and rejects a return to lost wholeness, though she criticizes industrial domination.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Haraway is enthusiastic about cyborg blurring of boundaries but insists on responsibility; mixed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Haraway's cyborg figure celebrates fusions of body and technology and 'pleasure in the confusion of boundaries'.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Haraway warns against command-control and coding the world as information.

restore-past-order.rationale: Haraway rejects appeals to a lost natural wholeness and organic origin.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The school holds that no knowledge is neutral, making a view-from-nowhere pragmatism questionable.

direct-action.rationale: Butler writes on assembly and protest as performative; adherents do not exclude parliaments.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Haraway rejects organicist return to natural wholeness and embraces technology.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Haraway discusses the changing division of labor but proposes no abolition.

production-for-use.rationale: Haraway analyzes women's work in the homework economy but does not state a position on production for need versus profit, so this stays neutral.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Haraway uses socialist-feminist labour analysis yet distances herself from totalizing Marxist theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Haraway criticizes Marxist unitary subjects and totalizing programmes; dictatorship of one class is contrary.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Haraway links militarism to high-tech capital but offers no inevitability thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: The school's left orientation and concern with welfare rejects the claim that taxes are theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Butler and Foucault question the neutrality of what counts as harm; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Butler's critique of fixed identity categories does not defend group rights, but she also questions liberal individualism; mild disagreement.

state-as-business.rationale: Haraway opposes privatization of public life.

media-academia-power.rationale: The school sees power as diffuse, but academia matters; the statement's framing as exceeding elected officials is a critic's claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Anti-essentialism rejects biologically fixed categories; Haraway and Butler treat race and sex as constructed and read through power.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation by fixed communities presupposes stable identities that Butler questions.

total-state.rationale: Haraway rejects totalizing theories and command-control; a state directing every area is contrary.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rejection of organic wholeness and nationalism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Haraway criticizes militarized domination and the school rejects natural national identity, so expansion by a strong nation runs against its politics.

bound-labor.rationale: Haraway criticizes exploitation of feminized labor; serfdom is the opposite.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The article states that postmodern feminists reject the God's-eye view, and Haraway's situated knowledges hold that all knowledge comes from a specific position; Foucault links truth to power.

universal-morality.rationale: The school rejects universals and grand narratives; Butler argues that identity categories carry exclusionary norms.

single-common-good.rationale: The article describes rejection of one universal account of women's experience in favour of difference; Butler favours coalition over a single good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Butler is critical of some forms of Zionism, but the school has no stated position.

rule-by-example.rationale: Moral example of rulers presupposes a unitary morality the school doubts.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial sympathy conflicts with scepticism of nation as natural identity.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The school critiques Enlightenment reason as a gendered universal, rejecting the claim that reason alone is the guide; but it does not endorse faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Haraway supports the welfare state and coalition across race; restricting to citizens conflicts.

class-collaboration.rationale: Socialist-feminist roots favour conflict analysis but not as a master narrative.

workers-nation.rationale: Haraway rejects natural unity and national organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The article describes the school as anti-essentialist about gender; Butler argues no universal gender exists, so legally distinct roles are rejected.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest-bearing lending is never discussed by the school's sources; no inference is available beyond a mild distrust of moralized economic bans.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Haraway grounds politics in coalition of women of color and affinity; classifying people by race for segregation is opposed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Foucault's diffuse power view contradicts the state-as-tool model, while socialist feminists accept it; split.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Haraway's valuing of hybrid and mixed identities opposes assimilation to one culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: The conspiracy claim conflicts with the school's analysis of power as diffuse.

national-mission.rationale: Haraway rejects the Western humanist self and colonial domination, so a nation spreading its own form of government is the hierarchy the school criticizes.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Postmodern feminists accept that women are subordinated, but Butler rejects a single universal patriarchy, so agreement is qualified.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Foucault's critique of biopower and normalization targets eugenic control, and the school rejects fixed natural categories.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Butler writes about state violence and precarious lives; accountability is consistent.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Haraway links the dismantling of the welfare state to the feminization of poverty, so confining government to defense and property protection is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hybridity, mixed and boundary-blurring identities are celebrated in Haraway.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Butler writes that some lives are treated as mattering less and calls for change, implying equality of worth, though she questions universal humanism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Haraway and Butler criticize colonial domination in general, but the sources do not take up the settler-colonial framing, so this stays neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Policing identity boundaries is contrary to the school.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a subject in the sources; a ban on religious grounds sits poorly with the school's wariness of norm-enforcing law, but this is a weak inference.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Haraway criticizes command-control and militarized state power, so a state growing stronger under siege is the opposite of her politics.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Butler defends popular assembly but the school questions the liberal subject presupposed in consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a group contradicts the school's anti-essentialism and coalition politics; Butler condemns persecution.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Butler favours nonviolence, but absolute property-based libertarian principle is foreign.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Haraway favours affinity, partial connection and responsibility.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Butler questions state power over speech while condemning neo-fascism; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: Haraway rejects totalizing Marxist unity and a single revolutionary subject.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Haraway treats women's work organizing as essential to resisting precarity, so legal limits on strikes would be opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Haraway locates poverty in institutions and the world economy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Haraway celebrates difference, hybrids and partial connection, so the claim that diversity erodes social cohesion is rejected.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Butler opposes state exceptionalism and writes on precarity.

party-controls-media.rationale: Haraway criticizes command-control of information, and Butler opposes censorship power.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrating command of the armed forces and ministerial appointment in one office is the kind of centralized command-control Haraway criticizes.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by scholars of a sacred text conflicts with the school's rejection of authority claiming truth.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Butler questions the state's power to define and suppress speech, and the school treats moral norms as constructed, so censorship for virtue is rejected.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Organic and natural-wholeness claims are rejected by Haraway.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Rejects religious claims but also treats science as situated; Haraway still defends accountable science.

restrict-pornography.rationale: MacKinnon-style restriction is a radical-feminist stance that Haraway criticizes for totalizing theory; postmodern feminists tend to oppose censorship.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based identity is the natural identity the school rejects.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Butler calls for troubling gender categories through performance and proliferating identities.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Opposed to authoritarian development; Foucault's critique.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Haraway names high-tech militarization as part of the informatics of domination, so national nuclear forces are opposed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Insulating monetary policy from elected government sits badly with Haraway's critique of technocratic command-control, though she never mentions central banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims grounded in a historic homeland are identity-based claims the school distrusts; the issue itself is not covered.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Haraway criticizes Marxist unitary programmes but does not take a position on how to classify the USSR.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Butler criticizes occupation in the Israeli-Palestinian case, but the general statement is not a postmodern-feminist theme.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The school is secular in outlook but wary of state power, and none of the sources discuss church-state relations.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sacralized hereditary authority rests on the fixed, natural order that anti-essentialism rejects.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Concern with the feminization of poverty favours progressive taxation over flat rates, an inference rather than a stated view.

character-from-environment.rationale: The article says the school holds that identity and gender are produced by language, norms and power rather than nature; Butler's performativity makes character an effect of repeated acts.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Butler opposes exceptional sovereign power and emergency suspensions, so a ruler above law is rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Haraway writes on science fiction and technology but sets no goal of space expansion.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass praise of a leader as the embodiment of the nation is the organic unity Haraway rejects.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Haraway criticizes Marxism's unitary subject but does not discuss post-revolutionary politics.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on shared nationality of people abroad rest on natural identity, which the school rejects.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Butler argues identities should be open to reinterpretation and troubled; punishing exit from a religion contradicts that.

women-must-cover.rationale: Butler opposes legally imposed gender norms, so a dress mandate for women is contrary.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity on ancestry is the natural identity that Haraway replaces with affinity.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The school gives language and discourse a constitutive role (Frug, Derrida, Butler), contradicting primarily material explanations.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Parity quotas rest on a category of women that Butler questions, but most adherents back equal representation in practice; contested.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A closed imperial economic bloc contradicts the school's boundary-crossing, anti-colonial stance.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Butler's nonviolence and the school's rejection of vanguards make armed foco strategy contrary.

history-own-civilization.rationale: A centrepiece of national or civilizational history presupposes a unified identity; Haraway's situated knowledges favour many perspectives.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Haraway criticizes the Western humanist self and colonial domination; rule over a 'less advanced' society reproduces the hierarchy she critiques.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Haraway sees capitalism changing form into an informatics of domination but offers no prediction about collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cultivating influence over former colonies reproduces domination that the school criticizes.

delink-world-market.rationale: Haraway describes global integration as a source of exploitation but calls for coalition across borders rather than withdrawal.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Butler's analysis of exclusion by norms and Haraway's coalition politics oppose permitted discrimination by private owners.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Butler's critique of juridical power and fixed identity categories cuts against entrenching rights, yet protections for the marginal are valued; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Butler defends democratic assembly, though she critiques the liberal subject behind elections.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Butler writes on protest and assembly as resistance; the specific constitutional claim is not covered.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The balance of monarch and parliament is not a theme in the sources, so neutral.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Haraway challenges the animal/human dualism and writes of kinship with animals; she treats the boundary as political, so animal suffering counts.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Haraway rejects dualisms and has ambivalent views on use, so adherents are split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist charity from the privileged is not how the school frames solidarity, which it places in affinity and accountability.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Haraway's cyborg politics is about responsible involvement, and Frug and Butler treat language and performance as sites of political struggle.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Foucault's account of power operating through norms and institutions rather than force alone matches this claim of consent through culture.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Haraway describes a global integrated circuit that exploits women in poorer regions, which is close to but not the same as dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving office by birth ties rights to natural origin; Haraway rejects this.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist claims depend on organic national identity.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The statement denies a settled historical point; Haraway's race-attentive coalition politics rejects it.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarization and Butler's concern with state violence make a political role for the armed forces something adherents reject.

paid-care-work.rationale: Haraway draws on socialist feminism's analysis of women's unpaid household and reproductive work and of the homework economy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Butler treats family and kinship norms as constructed, so freedom to leave marriage is consistent.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatizing pensions is the dismantling of social provision Haraway links to the feminization of poverty.

single-official-language.rationale: The school treats language as a site of political contest and difference; enforcing one common language contradicts it.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Foucault's view that power works through norms rather than intent supports judging by effects.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Haraway's critique of militarized command-control and Butler's concern with state violence oppose a great power sending troops to keep an ally in line.

corporate-influence.rationale: Haraway criticizes corporate and military control and privatization as domination.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Haraway and Butler analyze power as structural rather than conspiratorial and reject blaming a group.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Butler's kinship critique supports separating benefits from marriage, though same-sex marriage activism complicates it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Haraway favours affinity-based coalitions over unitary identities and fixed organisations.

religious-nation.rationale: A nation defined by shared religion is a natural-identity claim contrary to affinity politics.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist critique stresses capitalism's domination.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Haraway presents socialist feminism's analysis of women's labour and the feminization of poverty, implying economic change matters.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Haraway and Butler treat language as impure, contested and open to reinterpretation, so purging borrowed words is opposed.

majority-settlement.rationale: Engineered settlement of minority regions contradicts the school's anti-domination politics.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Butler does not discuss denial but condemns political atrocities; holding it false history is not postmodern feminism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Butler's critique of the heterosexual matrix and of norms enforcing compulsory heterosexuality opposes criminalization.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Butler defends assembly and critiques state censorship; Foucault critiques repression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Butler opposes state power to define and punish offensive speech, so punishing blasphemy is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Haraway criticizes colonial domination and the Western humanist self.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: This is an Islamic legal doctrine that the sources on postmodern feminism never treat, so no answer is given.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Butler's nonviolence and the school's rejection of fixed authority.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Butler describes public assembly as performative politics, matching direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The article says the school attends to intersections of race, class and technology; Haraway frames cross-race and cross-gender coalition as necessary.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The SEP presents Butler as holding a trans woman's gender is as real as anyone's, and Butler urges feminists to support trans and genderqueer people.

assisted-dying.rationale: None of the sources deals with end-of-life law; Foucault's work on biopower cuts both ways, so neutral.

alienated-labor.rationale: Haraway's socialist-feminist background carries Marxist labour analysis.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Essentialist claims about a civilization are what the school rejects.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority grounded in God is a foundational claim opposed to the school's anti-foundationalism.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Concern with women's subordination supports ending the legal silencing of harassment complaints.

rich-first.rationale: Haraway criticizes global hierarchies of exploitation.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Succession by descent assumes that rule is inherited naturally, a claim the school's anti-essentialism rejects.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Haraway links welfare-state erosion to feminized poverty.

property-franchise.rationale: Limiting the vote by wealth builds in exactly the exclusions that Butler and Haraway criticize, so adherents reject it.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Haraway says dualisms align women with nature to justify their domination, but she rejects organicist ecofeminism, so agreement on connection is qualified.

reification.rationale: The Marxist concept is not Haraway's vocabulary.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Haraway's critique of corporate control of communications supports it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Butler criticizes juridical power; liberal rule of law is not their theme.

racial-franchise.rationale: Haraway builds political identity on coalition across race, so voting limited to one racial group is firmly rejected.

open-government-data.rationale: Opposition to secretive surveillance and command-control.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Butler opposes legal enforcement of kinship boundaries.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority is opposed by coalition politics.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Haraway criticizes corporate concentration of power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Butler's critique of heterosexual norms supports equal inclusion, though she is wary of militarism, so this is weak.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Butler's views on state authority oppose imposing worldviews.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Haraway ties the erosion of public provision to the feminization of poverty, so reliance on private charity is rejected.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not stressed; the school focuses on present domination.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Butler's rejection of gender norms supports eligibility.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements are militarized, hierarchical organization of the kind Haraway criticizes.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Butler argues that sexed bodies cannot signify without gender and that the sex/gender distinction collapses, which the article calls the school's major departure from other feminisms.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Butler advises against defining 'woman' as the basis of feminist politics, and Haraway rejects an essential unity of women.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Butler's later work argues for an ethic of nonviolence but not as an absolute principle; the school has no rule against all lethal self-defence, so this is a mild inference.

second-chamber.rationale: The school has no institutional-design programme; its suspicion of unitary power points both ways on a second chamber.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Haraway ends the Manifesto preferring the cyborg to a goddess, rejecting both spiritual nostalgia and crude materialism; the school has no settled view.

gm-crops.rationale: Haraway welcomes biotechnology while criticising corporate control; no stated view on engineered crops.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Anti-essentialism and Haraway's affinity politics reject organising on a presumed fixed group identity, racial included, though she supports coalitions of women of colour.

racial-pride.rationale: The school is anti-essentialist about identity but supports anti-racist politics; no stated view on pride in ancestry.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The school rejects an essential 'woman' and any shared women's nature; Haraway rejects the natural unity of women, so distinct feminine values are denied.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The school distrusts unitary programmes and state control but proposes no strategy of smashing or capturing the state.

sacred-nation.rationale: The school rejects essentialist unities and foundational identities, so a sacred nation grounding lives would be refused.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Anti-essentialism is the school's core: Butler and Haraway reject a given human nature as a fixed ground of dignity, and Haraway's cyborg embraces redesign.

farm-price-support.rationale: The school gives no farm policy and Haraway's socialist-feminist outlook pulls both ways between state support and distrust of state control.

workers-own-party.rationale: The school rejects a unitary class or women category as the basis of politics, so a single workers' party is not clearly endorsed or opposed; adherents are split.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The school is silent on pollution law; it distrusts state control but also neutral legal categories.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses customary chiefs; the school is critical of power structures but also of universal models.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The school's politics is thin on environmental trade-offs; Haraway is ecologically minded but suspicious of programmes.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The school has no labour programme; Haraway's socialist-feminist writing on work gives no clear view on closed shops, so adherents are split or indifferent.

women-suffrage.rationale: Though it questions the category 'woman', the school is a feminism and treats women's equal political rights as settled; Butler accepts the rights while criticising the category.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The school locates oppression in gendered norms and power generally rather than in religion in particular, and adherents differ on religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: The school treats identity categories as produced by language, norms and power, and Haraway's writing attacks natural racial and gender categories alike.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The school is sceptical of state control and of institutionalizing the category 'women', yet supports gender justice; adherents split and it takes no stated position.

self-ownership.rationale: Haraway's cyborg and Butler's relational, interdependent subject dissolve the sovereign individual owner of the self, though Butler also defends bodily autonomy; low.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Haraway's cyborg writing embraces technology and rejects a return to origins and natural purity, so a return to ancestral values is opposed.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Butler and Haraway treat racism and its intersections with gender as ongoing structures of power, not as a past obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The school is sceptical of natural-law foundations, but Butler supports civil disobedience and resistance; adherents have no settled view.

multipolar-world.rationale: The school is anti-militarist and sceptical of unitary power but has no stated world-order position.

material-over-identity.rationale: Gender, language and identity are the school's core subject, so confining the left to material interests is rejected.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Haraway describes the dismantling of the welfare state as feeding the feminization of poverty, so cutting welfare runs against the school's analysis. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Cultivating influence over former colonies reproduces domination that the school criticizes. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Sex, and not only gender, is socially constructed.
missingStatements.rationale: Butler argues that sexed bodies cannot signify without gender and that the sex/gender distinction collapses, which the article calls the school's major departure from other feminisms.

missingStatements.text: Feminist politics should not be founded on a single, fixed category of 'women'.
missingStatements.rationale: Butler advises against defining 'woman' as the basis of feminist politics, and Haraway rejects an essential unity of women.

missingStatements.text: Political solidarity should rest on shared goals and chosen affinity rather than on a shared identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Haraway's 'affinity, not identity' and Butler's coalitional politics put solidarity on political goals rather than shared nature.
missingStatements.declined: Largely a corollary of rejecting a fixed category of women (no-fixed-category-of-women); kept out to stay lean.

notes: Most political-programme answers are inferences from Haraway (socialist-feminist, anti-militarist) and Butler's public statements; the school has no party programme. Strands such as Butler's trans-inclusive feminism are contested by gender-critical and radical feminists.
